name: Jacopo Sannazaro
bio: Jacopo Sannazaro (1458–1530) was a Neapolitan poet and humanist of a noble family, a member of Pontano's academy under the name Actius Sincerus, and a courtier of the Aragonese kings of Naples, whom he followed into exile in France in 1501 when Frederick lost his throne.

His Arcadia, a pastoral romance in which twelve prose chapters alternate with twelve verse eclogues, circulated in manuscript from the 1480s and was printed in its full form in 1504. It founded the European pastoral romance and was imitated by Montemayor, Sidney and many others. He also wrote Latin piscatory eclogues and the epic De partu Virginis (1526).
